turns.question: Should an invitation create membership immediately, or must the invitee accept first with an expiring invite link?

contract.G: Add team invitations without misrepresenting membership before invitee acceptance.
contract.T: Create a pending invitation flow that issues 7-day expiring invite links and only creates organization membership through the current membership service after the invitee accepts.
contract.S: Include invitation creation, persistence of pending invites, acceptance endpoint/UI, expiry handling, and owner/member role selection; exclude broader org-role changes and any redesign of the membership service beyond invoking it on acceptance.
contract.V: Verify an owner can send an invite, the invite remains pending until accepted, acceptance before expiry creates the correct membership, and expired links cannot create membership.
contract.X: Stop if the current system cannot store a pending invitation state or generate/validate expiring acceptance links without replacing the membership service.
contract.P: Persist through the smallest end-to-end invitation slice using the existing membership service only at acceptance time.

promotions.name: Invitation acceptance before membership
promotions.evidence: Repository only supports direct admin-created membership and has no pending invitation state, so acceptance timing must be recorded explicitly.

turns.question: When you say Account, should global search filter by sign-in identities or by billable organization accounts?

contract.G: Add an Account filter to global search with the intended domain meaning.
contract.T: Add an Account filter that narrows global search to billable organization accounts, not person sign-in identities.
contract.S: Cover search filter labeling, query behavior, and results limited to organization-account entities; exclude changes to authentication account search or person identity terminology outside this filter.
contract.V: Verify selecting the Account filter returns only billable organizations and does not surface person sign-in accounts.
contract.X: Stop if global search has no distinct organization-account entity/query path to target without redefining the search domain model.
contract.P: Persist on the smallest search-only slice and avoid unrelated auth-account changes.

promotions.name: Account
promotions.evidence: Repository uses Account for both authentication people and billing organizations, creating a direct naming collision.

turns.question: For the first version, do you need offline editing and later sync, or only offline access to documents that were already opened?

contract.G: Provide a truthful first offline capability for the editor.
contract.T: Make previously opened documents readable offline from the client cache without supporting offline edits or sync.
contract.S: Include caching and reopening previously viewed documents while offline plus clear read-only behavior; exclude offline mutations, mutation queues, and conflict resolution.
contract.V: Verify a previously opened document can be reopened with no network connection and is clearly non-editable offline; verify never-opened documents remain unavailable offline.
contract.X: Stop if the client cache cannot reliably persist full document content for offline reopen without introducing a new local storage layer beyond this slice.
contract.P: Persist on offline read access only and do not expand into unsolved sync/conflict behavior.

promotions.name: Offline mode v1 is read-only
promotions.evidence: Documents are server-authoritative, there is no mutation queue, and conflict resolution is undefined.

turns.question: When some CSV rows are invalid or duplicates, should import stop entirely, save valid rows immediately, or show a preview so people can skip bad rows before confirming?

contract.G: Add CSV contact import with safe handling of invalid rows.
contract.T: Build a CSV import flow that previews parsed rows, flags rows missing a required name or reachable address or having duplicate email addresses, lets the user skip invalid rows, and saves nothing until the user confirms the final selection.
contract.S: Include CSV upload, column mapping into required contact fields, validation, preview, skip-selection, and confirmed batch save; exclude background imports and automatic duplicate merging.
contract.V: Verify users can map CSV columns, preview validation results, exclude invalid rows, and complete one confirmed save with only selected valid contacts created; verify no partial save occurs before confirmation.
contract.X: Stop if the product cannot support a preview-and-confirm flow without first introducing any import UI surface at all.
contract.P: Persist on a single interactive import path with confirmation gating all writes.

promotions.name: CSV import confirmation model
promotions.evidence: No CSV schema or preview exists, and duplicate email rows are already rejected, so pre-save review behavior should be explicit.

turns.question: Who needs to log in, and do signed-in users need to be isolated from each other's data?
Should this use the existing identity provider only if it can isolate customers, or should login proceed even if tenant isolation is not available there?

contract.G: Add login in a way that enforces independent-customer data isolation.
contract.T: Implement customer login using the existing identity provider only if it can support user isolation, and add the minimum ownership/tenant model needed so customers cannot see each other's data.
contract.S: Include authentication, user-to-customer association, record ownership or tenant scoping required for isolation, and authorization checks on data access; exclude broader role hierarchies beyond what isolation minimally needs.
contract.V: Verify separate customers can sign in, access only their own records, and cannot retrieve another customer's data through normal UI or direct requests.
contract.X: Stop if the existing identity provider cannot support the required isolation model or if data cannot be tenant-scoped without a broader redesign than this bounded slice.
contract.P: Persist on the minimum secure multi-customer login slice and stop rather than shipping auth without data isolation.

promotions.name: Tenant isolation as part of login
promotions.evidence: No user, role, authorization, or data ownership model exists, so login scope must explicitly include customer isolation.

turns.question: For the first version, is an in-app notification sufficient when a build finishes, or do you need email or mobile push too?

contract.G: Notify users when a build finishes using an available delivery channel.
contract.T: Emit an in-app notification from the existing build-completion event when a build finishes.
contract.S: Cover notification creation, delivery into the existing in-product notifications UI, and basic success/failure messaging; exclude email, mobile push, and provider setup.
contract.V: Verify a completed build produces a visible in-app notification for the relevant user and that no external messaging providers are required.
contract.X: Stop if the existing in-product notification system cannot target the intended build user without first introducing a separate recipient model.
contract.P: Persist on the in-app channel only and avoid speculative multi-channel infrastructure.
